issues: Source CXLVI addresses the alleged kind and causal source of status, NOT whether a person actually obtains rank; distinguish from preceding CXLIIII.
The original printed CXLV numbering omission before CXLVI remains; no invented CXLV unit was added.
An eligible primary planet must partile-aspect one of the luminaries, giving precedence to the most essentially dignified light; original orb and arbitration algorithms are not supplied here.
The author gives numerous alternative alleged motives and people for each planet, not a deterministic occupational result.
Saturn is not always a bad outcome: when strong and aspecting the light, it allegedly signifies inheritance, possessions, favor or help from elders.
Jupiter/Venus's supposed honesty, gravity and virtue are period normative claims, not independently measured morality.
Mars's military status, Mercury's intellect/scholarship and Saturn's possessions are old social categories, not literal modern job predictions.
First house honors from personal industry and second house honors from wealth are separate alleged causes, not the same event as receiving a public appointment.
Two staged explicit fallbacks are given: if no light-aspecting source planet select strongest tenth occupant; if no tenth occupant use tenth ruler and its occupied house.

Lilly acknowledges an alternative reading from other astrologers considering a dispositor of luminary above earth or the most partile luminary/tenth-ruler connection; neither has an established priority for conflicts.
No verified personal career path, social baseline, historical income, birth-time record, outcome denominator, decoy or prospective evaluation appears in the source.
This is selective first-edition historical paraphrase and photographed provenance, not a diplomatic source edition or tested natal causal model.
The separately printed CHAP CXLVII begins after a horizontal divider on original PDF656 and concerns HONORS CONTINUING; do not include it as CXLVI.
